html:
The December murders were the killing of fifteen prominent critics of the military government of Suriname on 8 December 1982 at Fort Zeelandia in Paramaribo.

The victims, arrested the night before, included lawyers, journalists, union leaders, university teachers and soldiers. They had called for a return to democracy after the coup of Dési Bouterse. Their bodies showed signs of torture. The killings shocked the country, and the Netherlands stopped its aid.

For decades no one was tried. A trial began in 2007, and in 2019 a military court sentenced Bouterse, by then a former president, to twenty years. The sentence was upheld in 2023. The killings are remembered every December in Paramaribo, a reminder of the fragility of democracy in Suriname after independence.
sum: The December murders were the killing of fifteen prominent critics of the military government of Suriname on 8 December 1982 at Fort Zeelandia in Paramaribo.
